problem_statement: The CPU frequency scaling subsystem has no mechanism to constrain the highest-performance P-state based on temperature. A load-based policy can keep requesting the highest-performance P-state even when the die temperature is too high, risking thermal runaway. The subsystem should support an optional thermal cap layer that, based on configurable temperature trip points (with hysteresis), limits the maximum allowed P-state. When a temperature trip is active, the policy-selected P-state should be clamped to the cap P-state or lower (by index). Multiple active trips should apply the most restrictive cap. If the temperature sensor fails repeatedly, a fail-safe P-state (the lowest-performance one) should be applied. Recovery from sensor failure should recompute the cap from the next successful sample. The thermal cap should not raise a requested P-state that is already lower-performance than the cap.

problem_statement_fixed:
The CPU frequency scaling subsystem has no mechanism to constrain the highest-performance P-state based on temperature. A load-based policy can keep requesting the highest-performance P-state even when the die temperature is too high, risking thermal runaway. The subsystem should support an optional thermal cap layer, enabled by Kconfig option CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_THERMAL_CAP, that, based on configurable temperature trip points (with hysteresis), limits the maximum allowed P-state.

The thermal cap is configured via a devicetree node with compatible "zephyr,cpu-freq-thermal-cap". The node has the following properties: sensor (phandle to a temperature sensor device), sensor-channel (string, one of "die-temp" or "ambient-temp"), polling-delay-ms (integer, polling interval in milliseconds when no trip is active), and trip-active-polling-delay-ms (integer, polling interval in milliseconds when one or more trips are active). Each child node of the thermal cap node represents a trip point and has: temperature-millicelsius (integer, the temperature threshold in millicelsius at which the trip activates), hysteresis-millicelsius (integer, the hysteresis in millicelsius; the trip releases when the temperature falls to temperature-millicelsius minus hysteresis-millicelsius), and cap-pstate (phandle to the highest-performance P-state allowed while the trip is active).

When a temperature trip is active, the policy-selected P-state should be clamped to the cap P-state or lower (by index). Multiple active trips should apply the most restrictive cap. If the temperature sensor fails repeatedly — specifically, after a configurable number of consecutive sample failures set by Kconfig option CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_THERMAL_CAP_SENSOR_FAILURE_LIMIT (default 3) — a fail-safe P-state (the lowest-performance one, i.e. the P-state with the highest index in the performance-states table) should be applied. Recovery from sensor failure should recompute the cap from the next successful sample. The thermal cap should not raise a requested P-state that is already lower-performance than the cap.

The thermal cap exposes two public API functions declared in the header cpu_freq_thermal_cap.h:

- int cpu_freq_thermal_cap_sample(void): samples the configured thermal sensor and updates the cached thermal cap. Returns 0 on success, or a negative errno on failure (for example -EIO when the sensor read fails). Repeated failures up to CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_THERMAL_CAP_SENSOR_FAILURE_LIMIT trigger the fail-safe P-state.
- const struct pstate *cpu_freq_thermal_cap_apply(const struct pstate *state): applies the cached thermal cap to the requested P-state selected by the active policy. Returns the P-state to pass to the driver (clamped to the cap or lower by index), or NULL if the input is NULL.
